title: Irish Lamb Stew with Potatoes and Carrots
summary: Lamb shoulder is browned then slow-braised in the oven with onions, potatoes and carrots for a thick, simple, deeply comforting one-pot stew.
equipment: large ovenproof casserole (Dutch oven, 6 litres) with lid

ingredients.item: boneless lamb shoulder, trimmed of excess fat, cut into 4 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
carrots, peeled, cut into 3 cm chunks
waxy or all-rounder potatoes, peeled, cut into 4 cm chunks
fine sea salt or table salt
slices brown soda bread or wholemeal bread, to serve

steps.title: Season the lamb
steps.text: Heat the oven to 160°C (fan 140°C). Pat the lamb dry with kitchen paper and season all over with the salt and pepper; drying the meat first helps it brown rather than steam in the pan.

steps.title: Brown the lamb
steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large ovenproof casserole over medium-high heat and brown the lamb in 2 batches, 5-6 minutes per batch, without moving the pieces until they release easily. Set the browned lamb aside; the caramelised crust left behind, along with the browned bits stuck to the pot, will flavour the whole stew.

steps.title: Cook the onions
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining oil and the onion wedges, and cook for 8 minutes, scraping the base of the pot, until browned. Stir in the flour for 1 minute to cook it out slightly, then gradually stir in the water and stock until smooth.

steps.title: Braise in the oven
steps.text: Return the lamb and its juices to the pot with the thyme and bay leaves, bring to a simmer on the hob, then cover and transfer to the oven for 1 hour. The gentle, even heat of the oven keeps the stew at a steady simmer so the tough shoulder meat softens without drying out.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Stir in the carrots and potatoes with the vegetable salt, pushing them down under the liquid, then cover and return to the oven for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, until the lamb is very tender and the potatoes are cooked through. Check a potato chunk with a knife; it should give way easily with no resistance.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Skim off any fat from the surface, remove the thyme stalks and bay leaves, then stir in the parsley. Serve in bowls with slices of bread for mopping up the gravy.

tips: Pat the lamb really dry before browning; any surface moisture will stop it from forming a good crust.
A common mistake is moving the lamb around the pan too soon; leave it undisturbed until it releases cleanly from the base.
Cut the potatoes and carrots to a similar size so they finish cooking at the same time.
Scraping up the browned bits from the pot after browning the onions adds a lot of flavour to the gravy, so don't skip it.
Stir in fresh parsley right at the end to keep its colour and flavour bright.
storage: Cool leftovers within 2 hours, refrigerate for up to 3 days, and reheat until piping hot (74°C) throughout before serving.
